A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICGNN research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the six main benchmarks, OGBN-arxiv and Cornell evaluations, and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 newly states that training incorporates a negative-sampling reconstruction objective, extending v1's cross-entropy-only objective description. The ICS, GMM, correction, and pseudo-labeling procedures remain unchanged. Equation (8) and Algorithm 1 are not updated to specify the additional objective.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six main datasets plus OGBN-arxiv and Cornell on noisy semi-supervised node classification. Uniform and pair noise, label scarcity, and extreme-noise scenarios are retained; the added heterophily discussion introduces no new evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1, robustness and scalability experiments, and the twelve additional comparisons in Tables 8–9. DREAM is newly discussed as related work but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The documented experimental protocols retain the same splits, labeled-node proportions, noise generation, GCN backbone, accuracy metric, and 200-epoch budget. The appendix experiments also retain their settings; no new evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Component ablations, fixed versus learned alpha, backbone comparisons, noise and label-rate sensitivity, extreme-noise tests, and visualizations are retained. The new hard-node and heterophily discussions interpret existing evidence rather than add analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs, means and standard deviations, and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests at the 0.1 significance level. v1 Table 2 becomes v2 Table 5 with identical p-values; the added appendix subsection restates the existing testing procedure.

E6.justification: Matched tables and plotted results are unchanged, including all supplementary comparisons. For example, ICGNN retains 80.9±0.8 on Cora with uniform noise, 28.3 on OGBN-arxiv, and 44.7±1.6 on Cornell. Table renumbering and relocation introduce no new findings.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3.1 and its proof in Appendix A. Under column normalization and a joint homophily assumption, it derives clean-node ICS bounds of at most 1−delta and noisy-node bounds of at least delta. This introduces a formal justification for the central indicator that v1 lacked.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: influence-based noise detection, soft neighbor-based label correction, pseudo-label supervision, and superior benchmark performance. The new theoretical material does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: New Appendices B.3–B.4 explain purported distinctions between mislabeled, hard, and heterophilous nodes. Section 3.1 adds threshold-based motivation for GMM, and Appendix C discusses computational remedies when many nodes are labeled. Existing class-boundary and extreme-noise limitations remain.

D1.justification: The advertised code location changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository in v1 Appendix A to the named wayc04/ICGNN GitHub repository in v2's abstract. Existing hyperparameters and the explanation of gradient propagation are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds DREAM, a topology-imbalance citation, and graph-clustering references, while replacing several background citations, including Hao et al. (2020) and Luo et al. (2024). The central positioning against existing noisy-label graph methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 makes localized introduction edits, updates affiliations and publication information, adds acknowledgments, and reorganizes the appendices. Complexity analysis moves out of the main text, and related work moves later in the appendix.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged and its detailed caption shortened. The significance table moves from the main text to the appendix, and other tables and appendix figures are repositioned. All nine figures and nine tables are retained with unchanged empirical content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds explicit theoretical assumptions and useful discussion of computational scaling, but introduces unresolved consistency problems. Theorem 3.1 and its proof reverse Equation (5)'s mixing weights for general alpha, while the newly stated reconstruction objective is absent from Equation (8) and Algorithm 1. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. These documentation gains and mathematical or procedural ambiguities prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
